Page text: “In 2023, 23andMe was breached by hackers who stole sensitive personal information and genetic data of 7 million 23andMe customers nationwide, including nearly 900,000 Californians. While being investigated by a multistate coalition for unreasonable data security, 23andMe filed for bankruptcy and proposed to sell the genetic data and biological samples of its customers. The California DOJ objected to the sale because state law requires a customer’s separate and explicit consent before the sale or transfer of genetic data and biological samples. The sale was confirmed and DOJ appealed the sale order. Separately, DOJ filed a lawsuit in state court over 23andMe’s unreasonable security and misrepresentations related to its security practices and the data breach. On October 19, 2026, 23andMe agreed to pay $6,010,000 to resolve the DOJ’s lawsuit that it violated consumer protection and privacy laws arising from the 2023 data breach, as well as DOJ’s litigation challenging the sale order.”
